How.title: From order in, to parcel out, in one system
How.subtitle: Every step is connected, every scan is recorded, and the whole trail is auditable.

steps.title: Receive orders
steps.description: Orders from every sales channel flow into one queue, with stock checked and reserved automatically.

steps.title: Assign work
steps.description: The system groups orders into waves and distributes tasks by zone, urgency and carrier cutoff.

steps.title: Pick
steps.description: Staff pick along system-planned routes, scanning to confirm every item — less walking, fewer mistakes.

steps.title: Check & pack
steps.description: Scan-verify before each box is sealed, with shipping labels printed automatically per order's carrier.

steps.title: Hand over to carrier
steps.description: Handover manifests per carrier round, with statuses pushed back to sales channels so customers see tracking immediately.

sections.title: Context
sections.body: The customer is a fulfillment provider packing for multiple online stores. Most of the work is consumer goods with frequent orders and sharp spikes during marketplace campaigns.

sections.title: Before Packiko
sections.body: At around 4,000 orders a day, work assignment ran through the warehouse supervisor — splitting tasks, chasing statuses, firefighting on the floor. Come campaign season, backlogs accumulated and nobody could see where the bottleneck was. Adding people helped, but not enough to keep pace with growth.

sections.title: What changed
sections.body: The team moved the whole process onto Packiko — orders grouped into waves and distributed to staff automatically, picking and packing confirmed by scanning every item. The supervisor went from chasing statuses to watching the dashboard and shifting people to wherever work was stuck.

sections.title: The results
sections.body: The following peak, the warehouse handled around 20,000 orders a day on the same floor space. Backlogs became visible from the start of the day instead of surfacing as complaints, and the brands storing goods there got clearer status reporting.

cta.title: Want results like this for your warehouse?
cta.subtitle: Every warehouse is different — book a demo, tell us about your operation, and we'll tell you honestly what Packiko can and can't do for you.

story.title: Why we built Packiko
story.body: We watched Thai warehouses absorb fast-growing sales with manpower and the supervisor's memory — which works, up to a point, but not at thousands or tens of thousands of orders a day. Foreign systems tend to be expensive, complex, and a poor fit for how Thai warehouse floors actually run. So we built Packiko: a WMS the floor team can genuinely use, and the supervisor can genuinely control work with.
